Integrating the two in the numerator seeks to retain the broad cross-sectional strength of hard-book value while using collections to distinguish the long portfolio from accrual-heavy value traps.

NAME: Depreciation-Policy-Neutral Earnings Value
EXPRESSION: IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib,DELTA(dp,1)),MUL(prcc_f,csho)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms should outperform when earnings remain inexpensive after neutralizing changes in the depreciation provision.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: A decline in depreciation can mechanically support current income, so adding the negative depreciation change back to income reduces the valuation numerator; an increase receives the opposite adjustment. This converts the previously successful under-depreciation trap mechanism into a continuous, positively oriented yield without merely substituting EBIT for EBITDA.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Accelerating Supplier-Stretch Trap
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf,MUL(prcc_f,csho))),IND_ZSCORE(DELTA(RATIO(apalch,at),1)))

EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Persistent payable financing may characterize efficient negative-working-capital businesses, whereas an increase in APALCH intensity is more consistent with newly stretched payment terms. The temporal refinement is designed to separate that deterioration from the structural supplier-financing exposure that produced conflicting cross-sectional and portfolio evidence.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Tax-Timing-Neutral Cash Value
EXPRESSION: IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(oancf,txach),MUL(prcc_f,csho)))
HYPOTHESIS: Operating-cash-flow yield should be more predictive after removing cash-flow contributions from changes in accrued taxes.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Positive TXACH can make cash generation appear stronger because tax expense has been accrued but not yet paid, while negative TXACH reflects the opposite timing effect. Subtracting the signed component produces a continuously ordered cash yield that prices operating cash generation before temporary tax-payable financing.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Opaque-Accrual-Stability Sales Value
EXPRESSION: IND_RANK(RATIO(sale,ADD(MUL(prcc_f,csho),MUL(at,ABS(DELTA(RATIO(aoloch,at),1))))))
HYPOTHESIS: High sales yield should predict stronger returns when the valuation discount survives a capital charge for instability in opaque asset-and-liability adjustments.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The prior directional AOLOCH signal was unreliable because the item combines heterogeneous assets and liabilities with ambiguous persistence. Charging the effective purchase price for the absolute change in AOLOCH intensity tests reporting instability rather than imposing an arbitrary good or bad sign on its level.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Book-Value Accrual-Expansion Trap
EXPRESSION: IND_RANK(MUL(RATIO(ceq,MUL(prcc_f,csho)),DELTA(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act,che),SUB(SUB(lct,dlc),txp)),at),1)))
HYPOTHESIS: High book-to-market firms should underperform when net operating working-capital intensity is increasing.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The signed change separates cheap firms accumulating operating accrual assets from cheap firms releasing working capital, rather than comparing value firms with expensive firms. Excluding cash, debt, and tax payables focuses the interaction on receivables, inventories, and ordinary operating liabilities that can make book value vulnerable to future write-downs.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

VERDICT: flag

RATIONALE: This is a near-mechanical merge of two archive signals (Working-Capital-Ex Book Value plus the RECCH term from Collected-Cash Value) in which a one-period cash-flow flow item is added to a balance-sheet stock that is typically an order of magnitude larger, so the ranking will be almost entirely the previously tested hard-book yield rather than a genuinely new interaction.

---CRITIQUE Depreciation-Policy-Neutral Earnings Value---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The adjustment direction is internally consistent (a fall in DP lowers the numerator, penalizing income flattered by reduced depreciation) and it converts the archive's weak multiplicative depreciation trap into a coherent continuous yield, though the signal risks being dominated by plain earnings-to-price given DP changes are usually small relative to IB.

---CRITIQUE Accelerating Supplier-Stretch Trap---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: APALCH is already a first difference, so DELTA(APALCH/at) is a second difference of a noisy cash-flow detail item, and the change is a cosmetic temporal tweak to an archive signal whose portfolio alpha (+2.08 t-stat) already contradicted the hypothesized negative sign rather than a diagnosis of that contradiction.

---CRITIQUE Tax-Timing-Neutral Cash Value---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Subtracting the small TXACH timing item leaves the signal essentially the long-published cash-flow-to-price value anomaly, while inheriting the sparse coverage of cash-flow detail items — a large loss of sample for a negligible economic adjustment.

---CRITIQUE Opaque-Accrual-Stability Sales Value---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The construct is sales-to-price (a known value anomaly) with an arbitrarily scaled denominator penalty built from a second difference of the heterogeneous AOLOCH flow, so any result will be hard to attribute to the claimed "reporting instability" mechanism rather than to S/P itself.

---CRITIQUE Book-Value Accrual-Expansion Trap---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: DELTA of net operating working capital scaled by assets is the standard Sloan working-capital accrual, and interacting it with book-to-market largely rediscovers the documented value–accruals interaction while reusing the exact functional template of the archive's Under-Depreciation Book Trap with a different accrual proxy.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Collection-Rate-Weighted Cash Value
EXPRESSION: IND_RANK(MUL(RATIO(che,MUL(prcc_f,csho)),RATIO(recch,sale)))
HYPOTHESIS: Cash-rich firms should outperform when their cash-to-market discount is accompanied by receivable collections relative to sales.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: Cash-to-market and RECCH-to-sales are both dimensionless, so the accounting-quality channel cannot disappear inside a much larger balance-sheet stock. Positive collections reinforce cash cheapness, while receivable accumulation makes the score negative specifically for cash-value firms rather than merely adding a small flow to book equity.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Supplier-Financed Sales Expansion
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(DELTA(sale,1),MUL(prcc_f,csho))),IND_RANK(RATIO(apalch,at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms should outperform when sales expansion is inexpensive relative to market value and is accompanied by increased supplier financing.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: The positive portfolio evidence for the prior supplier-financing signal suggests that payable growth can represent valuable operating financing rather than distress. Requiring concurrent sales expansion distinguishes productive supplier credit from payment stretching, while using APALCH at its natural first-difference order avoids a noisy second difference.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Cash-Composition Book Value
EXPRESSION: IND_RANK(MUL(RATIO(ceq,MUL(prcc_f,csho)),RATIO(che,act)))
HYPOTHESIS: High book-to-market firms should outperform when a large share of current assets consists of cash rather than accrual-sensitive operating assets.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: The cash share of current assets measures the realizability of the balance-sheet assets supporting book value, directly reducing exposure to receivable and inventory write-down risk. This level-based construction uses broadly available balance-sheet data instead of sacrificing coverage to remove a typically negligible tax cash-flow item.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Unfunded Inventory Build Yield
EXPRESSION: IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(NEG(invch),apalch),MUL(prcc_f,csho)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms should underperform when inventory accumulation not financed by increased accounts payable is large relative to equity value.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: Negative INVCH denotes inventory accumulation, while positive APALCH represents operating-liability financing; their difference therefore measures the portion of inventory investment requiring other funding. Scaling this mismatch by market capitalization targets cheap firms absorbing cash into inventory without matching supplier support, using transparent signed components rather than an opaque or second-differenced accrual item.

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Short-Debt-Funded Accrual Trap
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act,che),SUB(SUB(lct,dlc),txp)),1),MUL(prcc_f,csho))),IND_RANK(RATIO(DELTA(dlc,1),MUL(prcc_f,csho))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms should underperform when operating working-capital expansion and short-term debt issuance are both large relative to equity value.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: Working-capital investment becomes especially fragile when it is financed with short-maturity debt, creating refinancing risk if accrual assets fail to convert into cash. The continuous conjunction changes the mechanism from a standard book-to-market times Sloan-accrual interaction to a funding-source test in which both accrual expansion and debt dependence must be elevated.
